items.title: Italian Competition Watchdog Launches Suno Investigation ‘Over Unfair Terms,’ Says ‘The Contractual Provisions on Copyright Deserve Particular Attention’
items.summary: When it rains, it pours and, in Suno’s case, keeps on pouring: Besides facing a number of stateside lawsuits as well as international copyright claims, the AI music generator is now grappling with a formal investigation in Italy over its allegedly “unfair terms.” The Italian Competition Authority (ICA) disclosed the pr…

items.title: Sony Music’s AI Slop and Deepfakes Crackdown Intensifies — Soundalike Track Removal Requests Reportedly Top 250,000
items.summary: Sony Music’s AI deepfakes crackdown is intensifying: As of September’s end, the major label had fired off north of 250,000 cumulative soundalike-track takedown demands. That concrete figure came to light in a recent Financial Times piece, which pointed to over 260,000 deepfake takedown requests submitted to various “pl…

items.title: Who Really Wrote Katy Perry’s ‘Hot N Cold’? A Bizarre Twist Could Derail a Dr. Luke Copyright Settlement In South Dakota
items.summary: A copyright case involving Dr. Luke enters settlement proceedings, but a third party has filed an intervention request, alleging an authorship stake. This week, in the ever-shifting world of copyright infringement lawsuits, two parties on opposing sides of a copyright infringement lawsuit involving a South Dakota broad…

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.title: Major publishers tell US Supreme Court they must intervene in termination rights ruling that “threatens the licensing of copyrighted works throughout the world”
items.summary: The major music publishers and BMG have submitted a new filing with the US Supreme Court in the ongoing termination rights legal battle involving songwriter Cyril Vetter. He recently told the Supreme Court to ignore the publishers’ doomsaying about this case - their new filing has plenty of that

tip.title: Split sheet firmado el mismo día de la sesión
tip.body: Los porcentajes de autoría se pelean cuando la canción pega, no cuando se escribe. Firma el split sheet con todos los presentes antes de salir del estudio, aunque sean amigos.

tip.title: Sign the split sheet the day of the session
tip.body: Songwriting splits get disputed when the song blows up, not when it's written. Sign a split sheet with everyone in the room before you leave the studio —even with friends.
